paragraphs.en: How can the train operators possibly justify yet another increase to rail passenger fares? It has become a grimly reliable annual ritual: every January the cost of travelling by train rises, imposing a significant extra burden on those who have no option but to use the rail network to get to work or otherwise. This year’s rise, an average of 2.7 per cent, may be a fraction lower than last year’s, but it is still well above the official Consumer Price Index (CPI) measure of inflation.
paragraphs.zh: 铁路运营商究竟怎么能为又一次提高客运票价找到合理依据？这已经成为每年都会如期上演、令人沮丧的惯例：每到一月，乘火车出行的费用就会上涨，给那些只能依靠铁路通勤或出行的人增加一笔沉重的额外负担。今年平均2.7%的涨幅也许比去年略低，但仍远高于官方以消费者价格指数（CPI）衡量的通货膨胀率。

paragraphs.en: Successive governments have permitted such increases on the grounds that the cost of investing in and running the rail network should be borne by those who use it, rather than the general taxpayer. Why, the argument goes, should a car-driving pensioner from Lincolnshire have to subsidise the daily commute of a stockbroker from Surrey? Equally, there is a sense that the travails of commuters in the South East, many of whom will face among the biggest rises, have received too much attention compared to those who must endure the relatively poor infrastructure of the Midlands and the North.
paragraphs.zh: 历届政府都允许这样的涨价，理由是铁路网络的投资和运营成本应由使用者承担，而不是由全体纳税人承担。按照这种说法，凭什么要让林肯郡一位开车出行的退休老人补贴萨里郡一名证券经纪人的日常通勤？同样，也有人认为，与那些不得不忍受英格兰中部和北部相对落后基础设施的人相比，东南部通勤者的苦恼受到了过多关注，而后者中许多人将面临最大幅度的票价上涨。

paragraphs.en: However, over the past 12 months, those commuters have also experienced some of the worst rail strikes in years. It is all very well train operators trumpeting the improvements they are making to the network, but passengers should be able to expect a basic level of service for the substantial sums they are now paying to travel. The responsibility for the latest wave of strikes rests on the unions. However, there is a strong case that those who have been worst affected by industrial action should receive compensation for the disruption they have suffered.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，在过去12个月中，这些通勤者也经历了近年来最严重的几次铁路罢工。铁路运营商大力宣扬自己正在对铁路网络进行的改进，固然无可厚非，但乘客如今为出行支付了如此高昂的费用，理应有权期待最基本的服务水平。最新一轮罢工的责任在于工会。不过，有充分理由认为，受劳工行动影响最严重的乘客应就出行受扰获得赔偿。

paragraphs.en: The Government has pledged to change the law to introduce a minimum service requirement so that, even when strikes occur, services can continue to operate.This should form part of a wider package of measures to address the long-running problems on Britain’s railways.Yes, more investment is needed, but passengers will not be willing to pay more indefinitely if they must also endure cramped, unreliable services, punctuated by regular chaos when timetables are changed,or planned maintenance is managed incompetently. The threat of nationalisation may have been seen off for now, but it will return with a vengeance if the justified anger of passengers is not addressed in short order.
paragraphs.zh: 政府已承诺修改法律，引入最低服务要求，以确保即使发生罢工，铁路服务也能够继续运行。这应当成为一整套更广泛措施的一部分，用以解决英国铁路长期存在的问题。没错，铁路需要更多投资，但如果乘客还必须忍受拥挤、不可靠的服务，以及列车时刻表变更或计划检修管理不善时频繁出现的混乱，他们就不会愿意无休止地支付更多费用。铁路国有化的威胁目前或许已经被化解，但如果不能尽快回应乘客有理有据的愤怒，这一威胁就会以更猛烈之势卷土重来。
